title.narrative: Strengthening Resilience in Agriculture, Livelihoods and Markets (STREAM

description.narrative: 1. Improved, more efficient and productive agricultural inputs and output markets2. Enable non-farm enterprises and smallholder farmers to capture greater value and invest in expanded economic opportunities through financial inclusion, stronger market orientation and economies of scale.3. Increase psychosocial capacities and social cohesion among communities and market actors

Sustainably move households out of chronic vulnerability and poverty by facilitating economic recovery and growth for smallholder farmers and non-farm microenterprises in vulnerable and conflict-affected areas of Western Equatoria

The Dutch/Norwegian funding will support the training and facilitation ocommunity agriculture extension workers in Greater Mundri, expanding access to relevant agricultural skills across all Bomas. This initiative aims to equip smallholder farmers with essential agricultural knowledge while continuing field monitoring and support for the farmers previously reached under the STREAM II programme. Additionally, funding will support the construction and promotion of storage facilities to enhance access for farmer groups and cooperatives, enabling them to build economies of scale, strengthen bargaining power, and attract larger buyers. The programme will also focus on supporting MSMEs and local entrepreneurs to further drive agricultural market development.

recipient-country.narrative: The STREAM programme actions is targeted in Greater Mundri, Western Equatoria state, South Sudan

comment.narrative: A total of 86 MSMEs utilized business development services, exceeding the baseline of 10 and demonstrating strengthened enterprise capacity through business skills training, mentoring, and technical support.

During the reporting period, 52 MSE participants (20 males and 32 females) were trained on financial basics, entrepreneurship, business planning, management, and growth. title.narrative: Objective 2: Enable non-farm enterprises and smallholder farmers to add market value and invest in expanded economic opportunities.
GERF 2.17 Number of beneficiaries with access to financial services: (a) firms, (b) people (all financial services), (c) people (digital financial services) [SP][EFSD]‡

comment.narrative: Baseline covers whole project period
Target covers whole project period

Engaged 2 formal financial service providers, and supported multiple self-help groups to enhance access to informal financial services for farmers. Financial service providers have reached 112 self help groups with 1767 members (1271 male and 496 female)

Project staff are in the process of conducting an assessment to determine the number of new firms and individuals who have opened accounts with financial institutions (Cooperative and Eden Banks), as well as those accessing digital financial services such as M-gurush, Digicash, and Momo.
The STREAM II project substantially surpassed its target, enabling 1,473 beneficiaries to access financial services, demonstrating strong progress in expanding financial inclusion.

title.narrative: # of MSMEs gaining new or improved access to markets and/or financial services

comment.narrative: During the reporting period, 60 MSME participants (14 males and 46 females) were trained to enhance their business and market capacities in Greater Mundri. The training focused on strengthening small and medium enterprises, improving customer satisfaction and client relations, and creating networking opportunities for peer learning and business growth. Additionally, farmers’ groups were supported to increase productivity and efficiency, thereby contributing to a more vibrant and resilient local market with greater availability of goods.
Target covers whole project period
Engaged with Financial Service Providers (FSPs), Input suppliers and Agro-processors establishing linkages with MSMEs/farmers. Trainings MSMEs is expected to commence in the next quarter

The project exceeded its target cumulatively, with 64 MSMEs gaining improved access to markets and financial services at mid term evaluation, reflecting strengthened market linkages and financial inclusion.
